messages:
tess (pm): quick RFC follow-up: we left some ambiguity around aborting staged activations for big delta streams. want to decide operator UX + safety boundaries today.

ian (eng-arch): agree. two axes: operator-visible checkpoint granularity (component vs shard) and how rollback is executed (reverse-apply vs snapshot restore). also need an auditable ledger for state transitions.

rohit (eng-infra): infrastructure preference: shard-level checkpoints. shard boundaries map neatly to transfer/chunk streams and minimize partial-file complexity. checkpoint at shard commit point only.

morgan (operator): shard-level is my pick too. for console UX: show shard rows with state badges (PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/PAUSED/FAILED/COMMITTED). collapsible by component. quick actions: pause, abort->rollback, resume.

anya (security): security constraints: ledger must be append-only and signed. any action that mutates activation state should produce a signed ledger entry. verifier must refuse activations that don't have a complete state chain.

ian (eng-arch): sketch ledger entry fields: shard_id, manifest_id, prev_seq, state, actor, reason, ts, sig_type, signature_blob. we'll include a seq number for ordering.

rohit (eng-infra): sample ledger entry (json for readability):
```
{"seq":42,"shard_id":"sh-sd3","manifest":"m-2026-04-05","state":"PAUSED","actor":"operator:morgan","reason":"checksum mismatch","ts":1799999999,"sig_type":"kms","sig":"BASE64..."}
```
we'll store entries as small CBOR blobs alongside the manifest index file to keep lookup cheap.

morgan (operator): nice. operational needs: 1) CLI that writes these ledger entries for scripted interventions; 2) console shows the signed entry details for audit.

tess (pm): retention default? we don't want to keep PAUSED forever. suggest default PAUSED TTL=7d, FAILED=30d, COMMITTED=90d, configurable per-customer.

anya (security): retention OK but audit trail must never lose the signatures for compliance windows. i.e., ledger blobs can be GC'd from hot store but must be archived (immutable) for configurable compliance window, e.g., 1y for enterprise.

ian (eng-arch): next: cache invalidation contract with serving plane. activation commit or rollback must emit an invalidate event with a signed invalidate token. serving nodes validate token before evicting prefixes. token fields: manifest, seq, ts, action, hmac.

rohit (eng-infra): implement HMAC with per-customer KMS-managed key. for private deployments, allow operator-local key with `sig_type:"local"` and mark it in ledger for auditors.

anya (security): local keys allowed only when escrow/attestation is present. Console should display amber banner if running with local keys.

morgan (operator): for rollback strategies: annotate manifest shards with `rollback: {strategy: "reverse"|"snapshot", snapshot_ref: "..."}`. default: reverse for tiny metadata shards, snapshot for blobs > X bytes.

ian (eng-arch): snapshot store design: content-addressed blobs, snapshot manifests reference objects. snapshots are GC-able and signed. create-on-demand pre-apply for risky ops.

tess (pm): UX question: when operator hits abort, do we show a confirmation that lists affected serving routes and estimated invalidation blast radius?

morgan (operator): yes please. also allow a dry-run that computes which prefixes would be invalidated without applying. CLI `--dry-run` should return a small summary table.

rohit (eng-infra): CLI example: `redwoodctl activation abort --manifest m-2026-04-05 --shard sh-sd3 --reason "checksum mismatch" --dry-run`
Sample non-dry run will output signed ledger blob and invalidate token.
```
$ redwoodctl activation abort --manifest m-2026-04-05 --shard sh-sd3 --reason "checksum mismatch"
WROTE LEDGER ENTRY: seq=42 sh=sh-sd3 state=PAUSED actor=operator:morgan ts=1799999999 sig_type=kms
EMITTED INVALIDATE TOKEN: token=eyJhbGci...
```

anya (security): add replay protection: tokens include nonce derived from seq and short ttl (60s). serving nodes cache seen nonces for TTL to prevent replay.

ian (eng-arch): reconcile with existing verifier: verifier will accept an activation commit only if ledger chain for all shards ends in COMMITTED with valid signatures. partial COMMITTED across shards is allowed but must be recorded.

morgan (operator): edge-case: what if operator aborts while installer is mid-write? we should define a file-level marker scheme: writes are atomic via temporary suffix + rename; tombstone only created at shard pause. reclaim GC will remove temp files older than a threshold.

rohit (eng-infra): agreed. temp file convention: `.tmp.<seq>` and final rename to canonical. GC policy: remove temp older than 24h by default, configurable.

anya (security): ensure signer metadata in ledger includes signer key id and algorithm (for audit verification). also include `sig_provenance` field when offline signing used.

ian (eng-arch): action items to add to RFC patch:
- formal ledger schema + CBOR storage spec (ian)
- manifest shard fields: rollback strategy, snapshot refs (rohit)
- console/cli abort + dry-run UX + confirmation UI (morgan + tess)
- invalidate token format + replay protections (anya)
- retention/gc defaults + archive policy (rohit)
- file-write atomicity contract and temp-file GC (rohit)

morgan (operator): i'll PR a mock console flow and a `redwoodctl` example output with a sample ledger blob.

tess (pm): i'll fold these into a follow-up RFC patch and aim to PR by EOD Thursday. sound good? :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: rfc/onprem-packaging-ux patch queued -> staging (id: d-4127)

ian (eng-arch): thanks. adding a note: please include at least one example rollback-playbook in RFC (operator runbook) with exact command sequences so oncall can rehearse.

morgan (operator): noted. i'll attach a playbook.

ops-bot: reminder: architecture sync in 1h — bring open ledger questions.

tess (pm): thanks all — will PR and ping when ready.
